text:
# Location and Size

Heybeliada is the second largest of the Princes' Islands (Adalar) in the Sea of Marmara, covering approximately 2.35 square kilometres across four hills, the highest reaching 136 metres.

# Historical Background

The island was historically known by Greek names referencing copper -- Halki, Halkitis, Demonesos -- reflecting its ancient reputation for copper ore.

# Naval Academy

A Naval High School, originally founded in 1773, overlooks the jetty and houses Byzantine church ruins, serving as a major educational facility for Turkey's maritime forces.

# Transportation

The island is served by Sehir Hatlari ferries from multiple Istanbul terminals. Horse-drawn phaetons provided land transport until 2020, when they were replaced with electric vehicles.

# Religious Heritage

The Halki Theological Seminary operated as the main Greek Orthodox seminary in Turkey until its 1971 closure; the island also holds several Orthodox monasteries and churches.
